sections.overview: The blue noddy is a Pacific seabird in the tern family. Molecular phylogeny places it as the sister species of the grey noddy, listed separately here as Procelsterna albivitta.
sections.identification: Adults are blue-grey overall, with a partial white eye-ring, a short slender bill and a shallowly forked tail; the grey noddy is paler, especially on the head and underside.
sections.habitat: It breeds on remote Pacific islands and usually remains near its colonies in coastal waters.
sections.diet: It catches small fish near the surface and also takes squid, crustaceans and insects.
sections.behavior: It feeds by hover-dipping or surface-dipping, often near other seabirds.
sections.reproduction: It nests in island colonies, using cavities or crevices in lava in Hawai‘i; breeding details are not well known.
sections.ecology: Its nearshore feeding and island nesting tie its life cycle to tropical Pacific coasts and colonies.
sections.conservation: The Hawai‘i wildlife authority reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern.
